headline: Technical glitch: Rooppur nuclear plant's test ops paused
summary: Operations were temporarily halted at Unit-1 after a fault was discovered during a 'cold run' test, though authorities describe the issue as minor.
details: The test operational process of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has been temporarily halted following a technical fault discovered at Unit-1 of the country's first nuclear facility.
The glitch was identified on Friday during a 'cold run' test while the system was being pressurized. Plant authorities have stated that the issue is minor and repair work is already underway.
The Russian construction authority has been informed, and a representative from Rosatom's PR agency noted that such minor issues are common during the commissioning stage of a nuclear plant.
Rooppur officially entered its operational phase after fuel loading at Unit-1 on April 28, with 163 fuel assemblies loaded into the reactor core by mid-May.
A series of tests are currently being conducted to identify and solve any issues before the chain reaction is initiated to generate power.
The halt occurs while a team from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is visiting the plant to observe its technical progress, though officials say the IAEA understands the process.
caption:
A technical glitch has paused test operations at Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant.

The test operational process of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has been temporarily halted following a technical fault discovered at Unit-1 of the country's first nuclear facility.

The glitch was identified on Friday during a 'cold run' test while the system was being pressurized. Plant authorities have stated that the issue is minor and repair work is already underway.

The Russian construction authority has been informed, and a representative from Rosatom's PR agency noted that such minor issues are common during the commissioning stage of a nuclear plant.

Rooppur officially entered its operational phase after fuel loading at Unit-1 on April 28, with 163 fuel assemblies loaded into the reactor core by mid-May.

A series of tests are currently being conducted to identify and solve any issues before the chain reaction is initiated to generate power.

The halt occurs while a team from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is visiting the plant to observe its technical progress, though officials say the IAEA understands the process.

headline_marked: Biman to [[resume Dhaka-Narita flights by July 27]]
headline: Biman to resume Dhaka-Narita flights by July 27
summary: The national carrier will restore the Japan route, with ticket sales opening on June 20 across all channels.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines will restore its Dhaka-Narita service by July 27, bringing the Japan route back into operation after a period of suspension.
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister Afroza Khanam announced the decision on Monday, noting that the government is working to ensure a comfortable environment for expatriates.
The route had been suspended from July 1 last year, citing aircraft shortages, Hajj flight pressure, and commercial considerations.
State Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat confirmed that ticket sales will begin on June 20 via the Biman website and other distribution channels.
The service will initially launch with one weekly flight to cater to the more than 40,000 Bangladeshi students and workers currently residing in Japan.
Minister Millat stated that the route had become profitable every three to four months before it was shut down, claiming the suspension was due to political reasons.
Japan's civil aviation authorities have requested 45 days to complete necessary security checks and inspections before the flights resume.
caption:
Direct flights to Japan are returning! Biman will resume the Dhaka-Narita route by July 27.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines will restore its Dhaka-Narita service by July 27, bringing the Japan route back into operation after a period of suspension.

Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister Afroza Khanam announced the decision on Monday, noting that the government is working to ensure a comfortable environment for expatriates.

The route had been suspended from July 1 last year, citing aircraft shortages, Hajj flight pressure, and commercial considerations.

State Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat confirmed that ticket sales will begin on June 20 via the Biman website and other distribution channels.

The service will initially launch with one weekly flight to cater to the more than 40,000 Bangladeshi students and workers currently residing in Japan.

Minister Millat stated that the route had become profitable every three to four months before it was shut down, claiming the suspension was due to political reasons.

Japan's civil aviation authorities have requested 45 days to complete necessary security checks and inspections before the flights resume.

#Biman #Japan #Travel #Aviation #Bangladesh #Dhaka

Source: Jamuna TV, bdnews24.com, Somoy News
